lead.headline: OpenAI's cyber agents found 948 ways to get root on Linux — and wrote the patches
lead.summary: In one mid-October run, OpenAI's autonomous pipeline (discovery → validation → exploit → patch) reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel bugs and produced 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits, at about $1.2M in API spend ($1,279 per LPE). Human researchers still review before anything goes to maintainers; OpenAI is shipping critical patches via Patch the Planet. The agents also invented at least 10 novel exploit techniques, and a hardened kernelCTF run still netted 21 LPEs for ~$33k — roughly 45× the historical bounty math.

number_of_day.label: API cost per working Linux LPE exploit in OpenAI's mid-October cyber pipeline run — total $1.21M for 948 unique escalations.

news.headline: OpenAI will buy Pierre Computer to deepen Codex's Git and code-review stack
news.summary: Pierre makes Code Storage plus the open-source Trees and Diffs libraries already used inside the Codex app. OpenAI wants agent-friendly source control; Code Storage stays available while its features move into Codex, and Pierre's open-source projects stay open. Closing still needs regulatory approval; terms undisclosed.

news.headline: Moonshot drops Kimi K3.1 Pro weights: 2.8T MoE, 104B active, 1M context
news.summary: The model that launched on 24 Oct is now free to download on Hugging Face, with coding and agent improvements Moonshot claims put it near GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 on some benches. License is mostly unrestricted; Model-as-a-Service over $20M/yr needs a separate Moonshot deal.

news.headline: Tencent's Hy4 adds vision, computer use, and long-horizon agents — weights soon
news.summary: Hy4 is live on Tencent Cloud and OpenRouter today; weights and system cards are promised in the coming days. First with GUI/CLI computer use and Blender/CAD training, same pricing as the preview (~$0.90/$2.70 per M tokens). Tencent says cyber evals found no serious offensive capability concerns.

news.headline: Vaisala Xweather ships Met-in-a-box: AI weather forecasts without a supercomputer
news.summary: First product after Vaisala closed its Atmo deal on 28 Oct. The box runs Atmo's AI weather model on local and Xweather observations, claims forecasts in minutes (vs hours), up to 100× finer resolution, and ~50% more accurate than classic numerical models — aimed at met offices, defence, and enterprises that want their own forecast stack.
